html:
Bwiti is a religion of Gabon that took its modern form among the Mitsogo and the Fang in the early 20th century, centred on all-night rites and on eating the root bark of the iboga shrub.

It grew from older ancestor cults of the forest peoples. Among the Fang, under French rule and missionary pressure, it absorbed Christian ideas, with Christ as a figure in the rites, and became a way of keeping community and tradition alive.

Initiates take a large dose of iboga, which brings visions in which they meet the ancestors. Bwiti is still widespread across Gabon and is seen by many as part of national culture. The plant's main chemical, ibogaine, is now studied as a treatment for addiction, giving the forest religion an unexpected place in medicine.
sum: Bwiti is a religion of Gabon that took its modern form among the Mitsogo and the Fang in the early 20th century, centred on all-night rites and on eating the root bark of the iboga shrub.
